rules.name: Unsandboxed Jinja2 Template from chat_template (CVE-2026-5760)
rules.fix: Render chat templates in a sandboxed Jinja2 environment (jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment); never render a template string sourced from model metadata directly.

rules.name: Streamlit caching of potentially sensitive data
LangChain tool with exec/eval
rules.fix: Validate LLM-chosen tool arguments against an explicit allowlist before execution; never let a tool directly wrap eval()/exec().

rules.name: torch.hub.load from user input
rules.fix: Pin torch.hub.load() to a vetted, explicit allowlist of repositories rather than a user-influenced path.

rules.name: Unpinned pip install in ML code
ML model download from dynamic URL
Fine-tuning endpoint without auth
rules.fix: Require authentication on any fine-tuning/training endpoint that accepts uploaded data or models.

rules.name: Model inference with raw file upload
LangChain structured object serialization boundary
rules.fix: Do not round-trip untrusted dictionaries through an object serializer. Upgrade affected langchain-core versions, keep untrusted data inert, and use an explicit minimal allowed_objects list when loading objects.

rules.name: numpy ctypeslib loads arbitrary native library
rules.fix: Load only libraries from a fixed, vetted install path; never build the library name or search path from model metadata, config files, or other untrusted input.

rules.name: numpy f2py compiles and runs arbitrary source
rules.fix: Never pass untrusted Fortran/C source to numpy.f2py.compile(); only compile source that ships with the trusted codebase.

rules.name: ONNX Runtime loads custom native ops library
rules.fix: Only register custom-ops libraries you built and vetted yourself; never load a native library that shipped alongside an untrusted ONNX model.

rules.name: Ollama server exposed on all interfaces
Triton Inference Server explicit model-control mode on public bind
BentoML runner server bound to a public host
llama.cpp server bound to all interfaces without an API key
vLLM OpenAI-compatible server bound to all interfaces without an API key
Jupyter exposed with no auth token or as root on a public bind
Unicode Tags block characters in source (ASCII smuggling)
Zero-width or bidirectional-override characters in source (ASCII smuggling)
Markdown rendering of LLM output without an image/link allow-list or CSP nearby
Raw reflection dispatch on a model-chosen tool name
pgvector similarity query built via string interpolation
Unbounded while-True loop with no visible iteration cap
rules.fix: Bound every agent/reflection loop with a code-controlled exit: a counter compared against a fixed max_iterations/max_turns, or a wall-clock deadline check -- never rely solely on the model's own output (e.g. a 'DONE' sentinel) to terminate the loop.

rules.name: Completion API call with no max_tokens/max_completion_tokens cap
rules.fix: Always pass an explicit max_tokens (or max_completion_tokens / max_new_tokens for the relevant SDK) upper bound to every completion call, and pair it with request-level rate limiting on the endpoint.

rules.name: Retry wrapper around a completion call with no attempt cap
rules.fix: Cap every retry wrapper around a completion call with an explicit attempt limit (tenacity's stop=stop_after_attempt(N) or stop_after_delay(N), or a counter compared against a fixed max in a hand-rolled retry loop).

rules.name: Embedding vector exposure on an unauthenticated route (embedding inversion)
MCP tool description built from non-literal content (tool poisoning / rug pull)
MCP server bound to all interfaces (0.0.0.0)
MCP server on SSE/streamable-HTTP transport without visible auth
MCP sampling request auto-approved without human gate
Unsandboxed Jinja2 environment constructed in serving/inference code
A2A server bound to all interfaces (0.0.0.0)
A2A AgentCard published without a security scheme
JWT/bearer token decoded without audience validation
rules.fix: Validate the token's `aud` claim identifies THIS resource server before trusting anything else in it: `jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=[...], audience=RESOURCE_SERVER_ID)` (PyJWT/python-jose raise on mismatch automatically), `jwt.verify(token, key, { audience: RESOURCE_SERVER_ID })` (jsonwebtoken), or `jwtVerify(token, key, { audience: RESOURCE_SERVER_ID })` (jose). Do not accept a token whose audience is absent, wildcarded, or names a different resource.

rules.name: OAuth redirect URI validated by prefix, or DCR-registered without an allowlist
rules.fix: Compare redirect URIs with exact string equality against a fixed allowlist, never a prefix/substring/regex match: `if redirect_uri not in ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URIS: reject()`. For DCR, validate every submitted redirect_uris entry's full URI (not just its hostname) against policy before registering the client, and reject registration if none are provided.

rules.name: MCP session id used as authentication, or generated predictably
rules.fix: Never treat a session id as proof of identity. Authenticate every request with a real credential (a bearer token validated per ns-aiml-159, or an equivalent), and use the session id only for session routing/correlation after that authentication succeeds. If you generate session ids, use a cryptographically random generator (`uuid.uuid4()`, `secrets.token_urlsafe()`, `crypto.randomUUID()`) -- never a timestamp or a time-based UUID version.

rules.name: OAuth wildcard resource indicator, client-supplied authorization-server URL, or missing PKCE
rules.fix: Never accept a wildcard resource indicator -- require an exact, single resource URI per token request. Take the authorization-server URL from fixed operator configuration, never from a client-supplied request parameter. Require and verify a `code_challenge`/`code_verifier` (PKCE, S256) on every `/authorize` request, public client or not, per the MCP authorization spec.

rules.name: PEFT/LoRA adapter loaded without a pinned revision or local path
Model merging / weight arithmetic without provenance verification
Airflow DAG run parameter interpolated into a shell/container command
MLOps artifact-store download without integrity verification
LLM cache configured without a tenant-scoped key
Semantic cache similarity threshold not set
Escape-grade Docker configuration for an agent/interpreter container
rules.fix: Never run an agent/interpreter container privileged, with the Docker socket mounted, or with host networking/PID namespace. Use a rootless, capability-dropped container (`cap_drop: [ALL]`), a dedicated bridge network, and its own PID namespace. If the agent genuinely needs to launch containers, use a scoped sibling-container API (e.g. a proxy that only permits a fixed allowlist of images/commands), never a raw docker.sock bind.

rules.name: Hosted code-interpreter sandbox with no visible network restriction or timeout
rules.fix: Set an explicit, short timeout on every hosted sandbox session, and disable network egress unless the agent's task genuinely requires it (e.g. E2B's per-sandbox firewall/allowlist settings, or your provider's equivalent). A code interpreter with an open network connection can exfiltrate anything it can read, regardless of how well the execution itself is contained.

rules.name: Sandbox inherits the full host environment or cloud credentials
rules.fix: Pass the sandbox only the specific environment variables its task actually needs -- never the full `os.environ`. Never mount a cloud credential directory or an `env_file` containing production secrets into a code-execution sandbox. If the sandboxed code needs to call an API on the agent's behalf, use a short-lived, narrowly-scoped credential minted for that one session, not the host's own long-lived keys.

rules.name: exec() presented as sandboxed via a trivial or empty globals dict
rules.fix: An empty globals dict is not a sandbox -- Python injects `__builtins__` automatically. Use RestrictedPython's `compile_restricted()` with an explicit, minimal `safe_globals`/`safe_builtins`, or better, run untrusted code in a real process/container/microVM sandbox (E2B, gVisor, nsjail, Firecracker) rather than in-process at all.

rules.name: Host root or home directory bind-mounted into an agent sandbox
rules.fix: Bind-mount only the specific project/workspace directory the sandboxed code needs, never the host filesystem root or a user's home directory. If the agent needs to read reference files, copy them into a scoped, disposable directory rather than granting broad host filesystem access.

rules.name: Agent code-execution tool with no recognized sandbox anywhere nearby
rules.fix: Never let an agent-callable tool run subprocess/os.system/exec directly against the host. Route all agent-initiated code execution through a real sandbox (E2B, Modal, Daytona, a locked-down container with dropped capabilities, or an in-process restricted interpreter with a genuinely minimal globals dict -- see ns-aiml-166).

rules.name: LLM tracing enabled with payload capture on
LLM tracing endpoint not pinned to self-hosted infrastructure
LLM tracing API key committed
rules.fix: Move the value to a secret manager or environment variable injected at runtime, never a literal in source or a committed .env file, and rotate it since it is already in history.

rules.name: Request-supplied media URL fetched without host validation
rules.fix: Resolve the hostname and reject the fetch when it lands on a private, loopback, link-local or multicast address (169.254.0.0/16, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, RFC1918) before issuing the request, and route every media loader in the tree through that one checked fetcher rather than re-implementing it per handler.

rules.name: Multimodal media URL read from a request payload
rules.fix: Treat the media URL as untrusted input: resolve and check the destination address against a private/loopback/link-local blocklist (or an explicit host allowlist) inside the single shared fetcher that every loader calls.

rules.name: Fake exec sandbox built from a restricted __builtins__ dict
rules.fix: Delete the dynamic execution path, or run the code in a real OS-level sandbox (separate process with seccomp/container isolation, no host filesystem or network) behind authentication; never rely on a restricted __builtins__ mapping.

rules.name: Unbounded multi-agent delegation topology
rules.fix: Cap every multi-agent delegation session with a code-controlled limit: GroupChat's max_round, LangGraph's recursion_limit (passed via config= at invoke time), or Crew's max_iter. A model-decided stopping condition (an agent replying "done") is not a bound -- a misbehaving or adversarially-steered agent can keep handing off indefinitely.

rules.name: A2A agent card fetched without pinning or signature verification
rules.fix: Verify the agent card's signature (or fetch it only from a pinned, operator-controlled source) before trusting anything it claims about the peer agent's identity or capabilities. Treat a remotely-fetched, unverified agent card the same as an unverified model download -- don't act on it.

rules.name: IAM policy with wildcard action or resource
Cloud logging or audit trail disabled
Overprivileged cloud service account or role
Cloud security group open to all traffic
Unsafe binary deserialization
rules.fix: Avoid BinaryFormatter/insecure deserializers on untrusted data; use System.Text.Json or a restricted XmlSerializer with a known target type.

rules.name: Docker socket mounted
rules.fix: Do not mount the Docker socket into a container unless absolutely required; if needed, proxy it through a socket-permission gateway that restricts the exposed API surface.

rules.name: ASP.NET CORS any origin with credentials
ASP.NET developer exception page in production
Go framework unsanitized input to dangerous sink
Hardcoded AWS credentials in workflow
rules.fix: Store the credential in GitHub Secrets and reference it as ${{ secrets.NAME }}; never commit a literal key to a workflow file.

rules.name: Hardcoded platform/API token in workflow
rules.fix: Store the token in GitHub Secrets and reference it as ${{ secrets.NAME }}; rotate the token since it is already committed to history.

rules.name: pull_request_target trigger used
rules.fix: Prefer the pull_request trigger, which runs with no write access to secrets. If pull_request_target is required, do not check out or run the PR head's code (github.event.pull_request.head.*).

rules.name: Third-party action pinned to a mutable ref
rules.fix: Pin the action to a full-length commit SHA (uses: owner/repo@<40-char-sha>) instead of a branch or version tag, so a compromised upstream tag can't silently change what runs in CI.

rules.name: Untrusted context value used in workflow
rules.fix: Never interpolate github.event.*.title/body, github.head_ref, or comment/review bodies directly into a run: script. Pass them through an env: variable instead and reference the env var from the shell, so the value is data rather than injected script text.

rules.name: Workflow input interpolated into a run: script
rules.fix: Bind the input to a step-level env: variable and reference "$VAR" from the shell, so the value is passed as data instead of being pasted into the script text.

rules.name: Pull request head ref interpolated into a run: script
rules.fix: Bind the ref to a step-level env: variable and reference "$HEAD_REF" from the shell. Never paste a fork-controlled branch name into script text.

rules.name: KV transfer control parameters on the public request schema
rules.fix: Strip kv_transfer_params, cache_salt and peer address fields at the ingress boundary, and derive peer identity in the backend from a signed internal context instead of the client payload.

rules.name: Internal routing header read from a client request
rules.fix: Drop internal routing headers at the gateway perimeter by default, and pass routing context to sidecars in a signed token rather than a mutable header.

rules.name: Cache key digest truncated below a usable width
rules.fix: Use an untruncated keyed digest (HMAC-SHA256 or BLAKE3) for cache and block keys, and never narrow the stored identifier below 128 bits.

rules.name: Unkeyed builtin hash used for cache key derivation
rules.fix: Derive cache keys with HMAC-SHA256 or keyed BLAKE3 under a per-deployment secret, and bind the tenant identity into the key material.

rules.name: Cache key hash seeded with a literal zero
rules.fix: Seed cache key hashing from a per-deployment secret rather than a constant, or replace the non-cryptographic hash with a keyed digest.

rules.name: fsspec ReferenceFileSystem renders spec fields as Jinja templates
rules.fix: Require fsspec>=2026.6.0 and never build a ReferenceFileSystem from a spec a user can supply.

rules.name: fsspec pinned below the ReferenceFileSystem sandbox fix
rules.fix: Raise the fsspec floor to >=2026.6.0.

rules.name: Jinja expression inside an fsspec reference spec
rules.fix: Strip Jinja delimiters from reference specs and only load specs you generated yourself.

rules.name: HDF5 external storage declares a filesystem path inside the artifact
rules.fix: Reject datasets whose storage layout is external before reading, or parse untrusted HDF5 in a sandbox.

rules.name: HDF5 or zarr artifact opened from an untrusted path
rules.fix: Parse untrusted HDF5/zarr artifacts in a sandbox and reject external or reference storage before reading.

rules.name: Unsafe ObjectInputStream deserialization
rules.fix: Avoid Java native deserialization (ObjectInputStream) on untrusted data; use a JSON library with a known target type, or an allowlisting ObjectInputFilter.

rules.name: Java MCP HTTP transport bound to all interfaces
Java AI provider API key embedded as a literal
rules.fix:
Remove the literal from source, load the credential from a secret manager
or injected environment variable, and rotate the exposed credential.

rules.name: Java AI/MCP tool description is non-literal
DJL model downloaded over HTTP without pinned integrity
Java model loaded from a non-literal path
new Function() code injection
rules.fix: Never call new Function()/eval() on untrusted input; use a proper parser for the expected format.

rules.name: Docker privileged mode or dangerous mount
Missing auth decorator on sensitive handler
Stack trace exposure in error response
Docker SDK container created with no isolation options
rules.fix: Pass explicit isolation options when creating the container: network_mode='none' (or an internal network), user= a non-root uid, cap_drop=['ALL'], security_opt=['no-new-privileges'], plus mem_limit and pids_limit. Mount the work directory read-only where the workload does not need to write.

rules.name: Another principal's identifier disclosed in a conflict error
rules.fix: Return a generic conflict message ('that name is already in use'). Never name the holder of the conflicting resource. Log the incumbent identifier server-side if operators need it.

rules.name: Caller-supplied header or metadata used as identity
rules.fix: Derive identity from a verified credential (a signed token, a mTLS peer certificate, or a session looked up server-side), not from a header the caller writes. If an upstream gateway injects the header, make the service reject the header when it arrives from anywhere else.

rules.name: exec() usage
rules.fix: Never call exec() on untrusted input; use a proper parser for the expected format, or ast.literal_eval() for literal data.

rules.name: Jinja2 template rendering from string
rules.fix: Never render templates built from user-controlled strings; use jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment if dynamic templates are required.

rules.name: trust_remote_code=True
rules.fix: Never set trust_remote_code=True on a user-influenced model path; pin to an explicit, vetted allowlist of model repos instead.

rules.name: AutoModel with trust_remote_code
rules.fix: Never set trust_remote_code=True on a user-influenced model path; pin to an explicit, vetted allowlist of model repos instead.

rules.name: LangChain loads deserialization
rules.fix: Do not deserialize LangChain objects (`loads`) from untrusted sources; use a safe data format (JSON) with a known schema.

rules.name: SQL string built with interpolated f-string
eval() code injection
rules.fix: Never call eval() on untrusted input; use a proper parser for the expected format.

rules.name: Unsafe unserialize()
rules.fix: Avoid unserialize() on untrusted input; use json_decode() instead, or unserialize() with the `allowed_classes` option restricted to a known allowlist.

Accept the credential only via the Authorization header (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or a POST body. If a query-string fallback is required for legacy clients, log a deprecation warning and strip it from any URL that is echoed back, redirected to, or logged verbatim.

Do not set resolve_entities=True or no_network=False on an XMLParser used for untrusted input. Use the default XMLParser() (or explicitly resolve_entities=False, no_network=True, load_dtd=False), or switch to defusedxml.lxml.parse()/fromstring().

Rewrite the group so repetitions cannot overlap: require a literal or disjoint separator between repeated atoms (e.g. `[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*` instead of `([a-z0-9_]+)*`), use an atomic/possessive group if your regex engine supports one, or validate with a bounded, linear-time check (a single non-nested character class with a length cap) instead of a general-purpose pattern.

Pass `httponly=True` on any cookie carrying a session or auth token, together with `secure=True` and `samesite="Lax"` (or `"Strict"`). Only set `httponly=False` for a cookie a first-party script genuinely has to read, and never for one that authenticates the request.

Pass `secure=True` on any cookie carrying a session or auth token, together with `httponly=True` and `samesite="Lax"` (or `"Strict"`). For Django, set `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True` and `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True` in settings. Only serve a cookie without Secure over a connection you know is never HTTPS, which for an authenticated app is never.

Use the `secrets` module: `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` for a URL-safe token, `secrets.token_bytes(32)` for raw key material, `secrets.choice(alphabet)` for a random character. Where an existing `random.Random` API shape must be kept, swap the instance for `random.SystemRandom()`.

Use 0o700 for a directory and 0o600 for a file the service alone needs, or 0o750/0o640 with a dedicated group for shared read access. If multiple accounts genuinely must write, give them a shared group rather than granting world write. Replace `os.umask(0)` with `os.umask(0o077)`.

rules.name: eval() code injection
rules.fix: Never call eval() on untrusted input; use a proper parser for the expected format.

rules.name: Unsafe YAML/Marshal deserialization
rules.fix: Replace YAML.load()/Marshal.load() with YAML.safe_load() (or Marshal with a trusted source only) for untrusted data.

rules.name: Unanalysed file path at filesystem sink
SQL injection via format! in query
FFI raw pointer without ownership doc

rules.fix: Send a safe format over the socket (recv_json, msgpack, protobuf) with a known schema; if pickle is unavoidable, enable CURVE auth and verify an HMAC over the frame before unpickling.
Bind the Listener to a Unix socket or named pipe instead of a host/port tuple, and pass an authkey so unauthenticated peers cannot reach the unpickle.

rules.name: Jinja autoescape disabled
rules.fix: Remove the autoescape block and escape the specific value you meant to trust with |safe, rather than disabling escaping for the whole block.

rules.name: Template value rendered unescaped
rules.fix: Drop the |safe filter, or sanitize the value with bleach.clean() (or the framework's sanitizer) before it reaches the template.

rules.name: Django csrf_token exempted in template form
rules.fix: Remove the exemption and include {% csrf_token %} in the form.

rules.name: S3 bucket with public ACL
rules.fix: Set acl = "private" and grant access via an explicit bucket policy or IAM role instead of a public ACL.
